answer: A bridge between cheap pseudonyms and trusted agents is a refundable stake: each identity locks funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. Reputation then grows only through verified work, and the zenith of trust is reached slowly, never bought instantly. A crystal-clear public ledger of stakes and slashes lets anyone audit the cost, making a Sybil flood expensive and visible before it can do harm.
